channel.title: Selected papers | Quantum Research Center
channel.description: Recent arXiv papers in quantum foundations, computing, and information, with explanations of their transferable methods.

item.title: Pump-Free Microwave-Optical Bell Pair Generation for Teleportation-Based Quantum Transduction
item.description: How can superconducting processors connect to optical networks while avoiding complications from optical pumping? Spin-mediated sources are predicted to herald microwave–optical Bell pairs at roughly 1–28 kHz, with fidelities of 0.86–0.99 depending on the platform. The pairs are intended for teleportation-based transduction.

item.title: Information Causality Characterizes the Set of Quantum Correlations in the Simplest Bell Scenario
item.description: Can an information principle recover the quantum boundary in the simplest Bell experiment? Generalized information causality implies the Tsirelson–Landau–Masanes criterion on the four renormalized correlators, so it recovers the quantum boundary of that correlator projection. A separate example shows that it also excludes some correlations that macroscopic locality allows.

item.title: Spurious quantum correlations
item.description: Can correlations that appear nonclassical acquire a classical explanation when the assumed causal structure changes? The authors identify correlations with classical explanations in alternative causal structures without fine tuning, and other correlations that resist such explanations.

item.title: Quantum error correction at ultra-low overhead
item.description: Can quantum error-correcting codes combine high encoding rates, tolerable noise, and feasible neutral-atom operations? Cornucopia codes reach encoding rates just above 1/2 at distances 6 to 18 and pseudo-thresholds above 0.4% under circuit-level noise. Their 12-layer syndrome cycle is carried out by rigid moves of whole atom blocks.

item.title: A solution to 2-copy distillability of Werner states
item.description: Can two copies of a Werner state yield distillable entanglement when one copy cannot? For every local dimension d, a Werner state \rho_\alpha is two-copy distillable exactly when it is one-copy distillable (\alpha<-\tfrac12). States with -\tfrac12\le\alpha<-\tfrac1d are therefore NPT but not two-copy distillable.

item.title: Quantum error correction with the toric code
item.description: Can neutral-atom logical memories sustain repeated error correction while replacing lost atoms? Twisted toric-code memories on 32 and 64 atoms ([[16,1,(4,3)]] and [[32,1,(6,4)]]) run for up to 90 and 70 syndrome cycles with atom reloading. Over four to eight cycles, the larger code has the lower logical error.
